quickAnswer: A private wooden boat day trip to Kekova takes you slowly past the protected Lycian Sunken City—where swimming and anchoring are banned—before docking at car-free Kaleköy to climb Simena Castle and swim in nearby bays like Tersane and Aquarium. Departing from Üçağız Village saves two hours of open-sea transit compared with Kaş Harbour.

body.text: What can you see at the Kekova Sunken City (swimming restrictions explained)?

Along the northern shore of Kekova Island, boats idle at slow speed past submerged 2nd-century Lycian house foundations, rock-cut staircases descending into clear water, amphora shards, and half-sunken harbour walls. Swimming, snorkelling, scuba diving, and anchoring are strictly prohibited directly over the archaeological zone to protect fragile masonry from fins and anchors.

Ancient Dolchiste slid partly below sea level after a series of major earthquakes in the second century CE, and the surrounding Kekova region is protected as a Special Environmental Protection Area alongside Türkiye's cultural heritage sites listed with the [UNESCO World Heritage Convention for Türkiye](https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/tr/). Captains navigate within a regulated coastal corridor so passengers can photograph submerged doorways and cisterns clearly from the deck—polarised sunglasses help cut midday glare. Swim stops take place safely outside the restricted zone, most commonly at nearby Tersane Bay (where Byzantine church ruins sit ashore), Aquarium Bay, and Burç Bay.
How do you climb to Simena Castle (Kaleköy) and try homemade ice cream?

Kaleköy (ancient Simena) has no road access, so private boats moor directly at wooden jetties below the hillside village. A stepped stone path winds past bougainvillea-draped cottages and family cafes up to Simena Castle in about 15 minutes, rewarding visitors with views over Kekova Island, Lycian tombs, and a miniature rock-cut theatre inside the ramparts.

Listed under the [Ministry of Culture and Tourism museums directory](https://muze.gov.tr/muzeler), Simena Castle charges €4 for international visitors in 2026 (paid at the hilltop ticket booth, or free with MuseumPass Türkiye), according to [Ada Yacht Sailing's 2026 Kaleköy guide](https://www.adayachtsailing.com/en/blog/where-is-simena-kalekoy-and-how-to-get-there-kalekoy-travel-guide). Allow 45 to 60 minutes for the uphill walk, castle loop, and descent. On the way down, stop at one of the village's family-run terraces for homemade goat's-milk ice cream (keçi sütü dondurma) flavoured with fresh peach, mulberry, banana, or bitter orange—served straight from small churns rather than commercial freezers.
Should you depart from Kaş Harbour or Üçağız Village?

Departing from Üçağız Village (a 35-minute drive east of Kaş) puts you inside the sheltered Kekova lagoon within 10 minutes, giving you calmer water and more time for swimming and Kaleköy. Departing directly from Kaş Harbour adds roughly 90 minutes of open-sea cruising each way, which suits travellers who want a full-day sea passage and skip road transfers.

body.text: If afternoon swell picks up in July or August, the return run back to Kaş Harbour can feel choppy for young children or guests prone to seasickness. Starting from Üçağız avoids that chop entirely and lets you finish with a quiet harbourside tea before driving back up to Kaş. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders work on a flat-fee, client-paid model—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions—so we help you select licensed local captains based on boat maintenance and safety rather than broker markups.
How much does a private wooden boat cost for the day?

In 2026, chartering a private traditional wooden gulet or day boat for two to six passengers costs roughly €300 to €450 from Üçağız Village and €450 to €700 from Kaş Harbour, depending on month and boat size. Rates usually include fuel, captain, deckhand, tea, and a freshly cooked lunch of grilled fish or chicken with Aegean mezes.

Confirm what is excluded before confirming your charter: cold drinks, beer or wine, Simena Castle entry tickets (€4 per adult), and round-trip road transfers to Üçağız are normally billed separately. Peak months (July, August, and Turkish public holidays) sit at the top of these brackets, while May, early June, and October offer softer pricing and quieter bays.

items: Verify in writing whether lunch, fuel, and soft drinks are included in the quoted charter total.
Bring grippy sandals or trainers for the stepped stone climb to Simena Castle (flip-flops slip on worn limestone).
Pack reef-safe sunscreen, polarised sunglasses for viewing underwater ruins, and a light windbreaker for the afternoon return.
Confirm your captain avoids noisy party-boat bays during peak 12:30–14:30 lunch hours.

faq.q: Can you kayak over the Kekova Sunken City?
faq.a: Guided sea-kayaking tours from Üçağız paddle along the outer edge of the Sunken City corridor under Coast Guard and archaeological rules. Kayakers are not allowed to land on Kekova Island's protected ruins or jump in to swim over the sunken structures.

faq.q: Is Kaleköy worth staying overnight instead of just visiting by boat?
faq.a: Yes, if you want utter stillness. Once day boats leave around 16:30, Kaleköy's handful of family-run pensions and waterfront tables become remarkably peaceful, accessible only by water taxi from Üçağız.

faq.q: What time of day is best to view the Sunken City?
faq.a: Morning light between 09:30 and 11:30 offers the clearest visibility into the water before afternoon breezes create surface ripples.

faq.q: Are there bathrooms and shade on Kekova private wooden boats?
faq.a: Standard licensed wooden day boats in Kaş and Üçağız feature a full shaded aft deck, cushioned sunbeds on the bow, a freshwater rinse shower, and an onboard marine toilet.

faq.q: How far is Kekova from Antalya or Dalaman airports?
faq.a: Kaş and Üçağız sit roughly 2.5 to 3 hours by road from Dalaman Airport (DLM) and about 3 to 3.5 hours from Antalya Airport (AYT).

faq.q: Can you visit Kekova in April or November?
faq.a: Private boats operate in April and November whenever sea conditions are calm, though water temperatures hover around 18–21°C and some Kaleköy cafes close for winter after mid-November.
